cosy-lesson.title: Inside the Backrooms: The Internet's Creepiest Place

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

p.em: Example: Empty buildings at night look very creepy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Space – a physical area or room.

p.em: Example: We need a quiet space to read books.

cosy-blockquote.p: Explore – to travel around a place to learn about it.

p.em: Example: I love to explore old castles and parks.

cosy-blockquote.p: Mystery – something strange that is hard to explain.

p.em: Example: The old house had a dark and interesting mystery.

cosy-blockquote.p: Exit – a way out of a room or building.

p.em: Example: Please find the red exit sign in case of an emergency.
Example: The internet helps us study and learn languages at home.
Example: Scary movies are very popular on Halloween.
Example: The yellow hallways are fake, but the museum is real.

cosy-blockquote.p: Lonely – sad because you are alone.

p.em: Example: A massive empty office can feel very lonely.

cosy-blockquote.p: Wall – a physical side of a room.

p.em: Example: They painted the bedroom wall a soft blue color.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
According to the article, why do millions of teenagers find the "Backrooms" so creepy and fascinating?
※ Have you ever had a scary dream about a repeating, endless maze?

How does the study define a "liminal" space and its psychological effect?
※ What is your favorite physical space in your home to relax in?

Why did the research team decide to explore virtual yellow hallways?
※ If you could explore any secret underground passage, would you do it?

According to the article, how does the mystery of the Backrooms make people feel both scared and calm?
※ Do you like reading mystery novels or solving puzzles?

What happens in the game when players cannot find a physical exit?
※ Have you ever been lost in a large mall or parking lot?

According to the paper, how did the internet turn a single yellow photo into a massive cultural project?
※ What is your favorite website to learn new things?

Why are empty hallways becoming a highly popular style for computer game designers?
※ Do you play popular online games with your friends?

Based on the text, did scientists build a real physical yellow room for their trials?
※ Would you visit a real museum of internet scary stories?

According to the paper, why do empty office rooms make people feel lonely and anxious?
※ Do you enjoy spending a quiet evening alone, or do you feel lonely quickly?

How does the article describe the yellow wallpaper on every repeating wall?
※ What color are the walls in your living room?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Imagine future research proves that viewing yellow hallways on screens is a creepy but safe way to cure real-world phobias.
※ Would you watch scary yellow offices if a psychologist told you it was healthy?

As our understanding of this scientific breakthrough develops, every office space will be designed with colorful patterns to avoid mental fatigue.
※ Do you prefer colorful offices or minimalist white ones?

Imagine biotechnology allows us to explore our own subconscious dream spaces using virtual reality headsets.
※ Would you like to record and watch your dreams on your computer?

If future research continues to support this discovery, we will solve the mystery of why repeating patterns make humans feel calm.
※ Do you find repeating geometric wallpapers to be relaxing?

Imagine future museums build a yellow maze where there is only one secret exit for brave tourists.
※ Would you pay to enter a real yellow maze with no visible exit?

As our understanding of this scientific breakthrough develops, the internet will become the primary place where new architectural styles are tested.
※ Do you think virtual houses will look better than real-world buildings?

Imagine future hotels become highly popular by copying the endless hallway style of the Backrooms.
※ Would you stay in a hotel that looked like an internet mystery hallway?

If future research continues to support this hypothesis (e.g. scientific prediction about spatial perception), we will build real physical cities that look like repeating geometric labyrinths.
※ Would you feel lost living in a perfectly geometric modern city?

As our understanding of this scientific breakthrough develops, we will prove that lonely virtual spaces increase our creativity.
※ Do you write or paint better when you are completely alone?

Imagine biotechnology allows us to project virtual paintings onto any physical wall using our brainwaves.
※ If your wall could show your feelings, what image would it display right now?

ul.li: Incorrect: Endless halls make me to feel lonely. → Correct: Endless halls make me feel lonely. ((Underlined error: causative 'make' requires a bare infinitive without 'to'))
Incorrect: This photo is very popular on the internet. → Correct: This photo is very popular on the internet. ((Underlined structure is correct! Good usage of preposition 'on'))
Incorrect: I am scared about empty offices. → Correct: I am scared of empty offices / frightened by empty offices. ((Underlined error: 'scared' is followed by preposition 'of' rather than 'about'))
